sections.h2: How do I convert WebP to JPG without uploading?
sections.html: Drop the files on this page: it reads and converts them in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, so it works with private photos, and offline once the page has loaded. Download each JPG, or use Download all.

sections.h2: Should I pick JPG or PNG?
sections.html: JPG for photos: small files that every app and upload form takes. PNG for logos, screenshots and anything with a transparent background, since JPG has no transparency. For those, use WebP to PNG.

sections.h2: Why do I have WebP files at all?
sections.html: Because the site sent WebP, and your browser saved exactly that, even when the address ended in .jpg. See why Chrome saves images as WebP.

sections.h2: What happens to animated WebP?
sections.html: JPG holds one picture, so an animated WebP becomes its first frame. To keep it moving, pick GIF in the menu above (in Chrome, Edge and Firefox), or see how to save an animated WebP as a GIF.

sections.h2: Can I skip the WebP file next time?
sections.html: Yes. With the Imgkeep extension, right-click the image on the web page and choose Imgkeep › JPG: you get the JPG straight away. More in how to save WebP as JPG or PNG.

faq.q: Does converting WebP to JPG lose quality?
faq.a: A little, as with any JPG: it compresses again. At the default quality of 92 the difference is usually invisible. For an exact copy of every pixel, convert to PNG instead.

faq.q: Can I just rename .webp to .jpg?
faq.a: No. Renaming changes the name, not the file: it's still WebP inside, and apps that refuse WebP will still refuse it. Convert it instead.

faq.q: How many files can I convert at once?
faq.a: Up to 20 at a time, each up to 50 MB. Drop more and the first 20 are converted.

pairs.card: Need a JPG for an upload form or a photo workflow? Choose JPG, add your WebP image and download the result. Transparent areas get a background colour; pick PNG when you need to keep transparency.

sections.h2: When is JPG better?

sections.h2: Is the transparency really kept?

sections.h2: How do I keep an animation?
sections.html: PNG holds one picture, so an animated WebP becomes its first frame. Pick GIF in the menu above to keep the motion (in Chrome, Edge and Firefox; GIFs are at most 800 px wide and 600 frames), or see how to save an animated WebP as a GIF.

sections.h2: Can I paste it into Canva, Figma or Google Slides?
sections.html: Yes: use Copy as PNG on the result and paste it. Google Slides and Docs don't list WebP among the formats they take, and PNG works everywhere. More in getting an image into Canva, Figma or Google Slides.

faq.q: Does WebP to PNG lose quality?
faq.a: No. PNG is lossless, so the PNG shows exactly what the WebP showed.

faq.q: Why won't Google Slides take my WebP?
faq.a: Google's help lists PNG, JPG and GIF for images, not WebP. Convert to PNG, or copy the result as PNG and paste it.

faq.q: Can I make the PNG smaller?
faq.a: Yes: set a maximum width before converting, or convert to JPG if the image has no transparency.

pairs.card: PNG is right for screenshots, graphics and images that need transparency. Convert a WebP to PNG when your next app needs it. Changing formats doesn't bring back detail the original already lost.

sections.html: PNG for graphics, screenshots and anything with a transparent background: it keeps every pixel. JPG for photos you want to share or upload, since the file is much smaller: use AVIF to JPG.

sections.h2: Why is the PNG so much bigger than the AVIF?
sections.html: AVIF is one of the most efficient image formats; PNG saves every pixel without discarding anything. The picture looks the same, but the PNG can be many times the size. Set a Maximum width in Advanced options if it's too big.

faq.q: Does converting AVIF to PNG lose quality?
faq.a: No. The PNG holds exactly the pixels the AVIF shows. It can't add detail the AVIF's compression removed.

faq.q: Does it keep transparency?
faq.a: Yes. Transparent areas in the AVIF stay transparent in the PNG.

faq.q: What about animated AVIF?
faq.a: PNG here keeps only the first frame. Choose GIF to keep the animation; see AVIF to GIF.

sections.h2: Why do I have animated WebP files?
sections.html: Many sites now send animations as WebP instead of GIF because the files are smaller, but plenty of apps and chats still play only GIF. See how to save an animated WebP as a GIF.

sections.h2: Can I skip the WebP file next time?

faq.q: Why is my GIF still?
faq.a: Either the WebP has only one frame, or your browser can't read animation frames. Use current Chrome, Edge or Firefox to keep the motion.

faq.q: Why is the GIF bigger than the WebP?
faq.a: GIF is a much older format and compresses less well, so the same animation usually takes more space. Set a smaller maximum width for a smaller file.

faq.q: Can I convert a still WebP to GIF?
faq.a: Yes, you get a one-frame GIF. For still images, PNG or JPG are usually better: see WebP to PNG.

sections.h2: Why convert AVIF to GIF?
sections.html: AVIF animations are tiny and look good, but outside browsers almost nothing plays them: chat apps, presentation software and many social sites expect GIF. Converting gives you a file that plays everywhere, at the cost of a bigger file and fewer colours.

sections.h2: How do I keep the GIF small?
sections.html: Set a Maximum width in Advanced options: halving the width makes the GIF roughly four times smaller. Short loops with few colours stay smallest. Very long or large animations stop at 600 frames or about 150 million pixels in total.

sections.h2: What about a still AVIF?
sections.html: It becomes a one-frame GIF. For still images PNG or JPG are better: see AVIF to PNG or AVIF to JPG.

faq.q: Does the GIF keep the AVIF's timing?
faq.a: Yes. Each frame keeps its own delay, so the animation plays at the same speed.

faq.q: Why does the GIF look grainier?
faq.a: GIF can show only 256 colours per frame, while AVIF has millions. Gradients and photos show it most.

faq.q: Does it work in Safari?
faq.a: Safari makes a still GIF of the first frame. Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox to keep the animation.

sections.h2: Can't I just rename .jfif to .jpg?
sections.html: Yes, for one or two files that's the quickest fix, and it loses nothing: the picture inside is already a JPEG. This page helps when you have many files, when you can't see file endings, or when you also want to resize or shrink them. It saves a fresh JPG at the quality you choose.

sections.h2: Why do I get JFIF files?
sections.html: On some Windows computers, a registry setting tells browsers to name downloaded JPEGs with the .jfif ending. See why Chrome saves images as JFIF for the permanent fix.

sections.h2: Can I stop getting JFIF files?

faq.q: Is JFIF the same as JPG?
faq.a: Yes. JFIF is one of the standard ways JPEG images are stored, so a .jfif file is a JPEG with a different ending.

faq.q: Does converting lower the quality?

faq.q: Can I convert JFIF to PNG?

faq.q: Why is the PNG so big?

faq.q: Can I convert many .jfif files at once?

sections.h2: When do I need a PDF instead of a JPG?

faq.q: Does the PDF lower the photo's quality?
faq.a: The photo is saved inside the PDF as a JPEG at quality 92 unless you change it, so the difference is usually invisible.

faq.q: Is my document uploaded anywhere?

faq.q: Can I make a PDF from a PNG?
